subject.title: RFC: Per-session tool policies — bridging operator scopes and agent tool access

question: Should OpenClaw bridge gateway operator scopes into agent tool-policy resolution with a new `toolsByScope` config surface, or should this remain part of session-envelope, sender/group policy, or tenant-RBAC work?
rationale: The choice changes the documented gateway trust boundary and public config contract, so code inspection cannot safely decide the product/security semantics.

options.title: Design scope-aware tool policy
options.body: Accept a new typed `toolsByScope` or equivalent layer and require docs, schema, precedence, upgrade, and security proof before implementation.

options.title: Route to session/tenant work
options.body: Keep this RFC as related context and make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/74632 or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87734 own the remaining authorization model.

options.title: Keep separate trust boundaries
options.body: Decline scope-to-tool bridging in core and continue recommending separate gateways or existing sender/group policies for mixed-trust deployments.

recommendation.title: Design scope-aware tool policy
recommendation.body: Accept a new typed `toolsByScope` or equivalent layer and require docs, schema, precedence, upgrade, and security proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter appears in the freshest trust-boundary and tool-policy history and is the clearest routing candidate for this security/product choice.
